text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Serbia's opposition coalition "Zajedno" bans the broadcasting of Croatian Radio Televison (HRT) program in Yugoslavia's norhtern province of Vojvodina, where a Croat minority lives.
- Privredna Banka Zagreb re-introduces interest rates for a vista and giro accounts which will be 2.5 percent annually.

- In an interview for the American weekly Defence News, president Franjo Tudjman proposes the 'Scandinavisation of the region', as opposed to attempts at unificiation, as a model for stability in the Balkans.
- Kaptol Proinvest, the first Croatian private open investment fund has accumulated some two million kuna over the first three months of its existence.
- President Franjo Tudjman has named Nenad Porges the new economy minister. Porges is to officially take up his post on April 15.

- The foreign currency and kuna savings in commercial banks have been doubled in 1996, while in the month between December 1996 and January 1997 the foreign currency deposits have grown by 1,391 million kuna and the kuna ones have been up by 114 million kuna.
- The currently established association of owners of family-run hotels and small guest houses is to offer tourists some 301,000 registered beds this season.

- Croatia strongly opposes Belgrade's request for control of airspace deep into Croatian territory. This represents yet another stumbling block in the normalisation of mutual relations, an editorial comment says.
- Croatian foreign debt totals some $4.8 billion dollars. The country has no prolbem repaying it, but the debt is high enough to deter taking further foreign loans. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
